evidence.text: 爺 is analyzed as 从父、耶聲, with original sense ‘father’. The entry cites Mulan Poetry for the father sense, Old Book of Tang for an honorific for men of rank, and a Ming Wan-shu za-ji citation for ‘祖曰爺’ (grandfather). These are dictionary-reported textual citations, not direct manuscript checks; the list does not by itself date when each sense arose.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 - 字頭「爺」

evidence.text: Reports 爺 and its proposed phonetic 耶 in the Zhengzhang system (2003) as Old Chinese /*laː/; explicitly lists 耶 as the phonetic component for 爺. This secondary summary supports a same-system sound comparison, but does not independently demonstrate the reconstruction or establish when the compound was formed.
evidence.title: 爺 - Wiktionary

evidence.field: Middle Chinese and Old Chinese readings
evidence.text: For 耶, gives Middle Chinese Baxter transcription yae, fanqie 以遮切, expected Mandarin yé and Cantonese je4, and Zhengzhang Old Chinese /*laː/. It separately describes 耶 as a corrupted俗字 of 邪; that account concerns 耶’s graphic history and does not establish that 爺 itself is corrupt or that 爺 was borrowed wholesale for another word.
evidence.title: 耶 - Wiktionary

evidence.text: States that 爷 is simplified from 爺 under the PRC’s 1956 Chinese Character Simplification Scheme. This supports classifying 爺 as the traditional counterpart and 爷 as the standardized simplified form; the exact relevant row of the primary scheme was not verified in this run.
evidence.title: 爷 - Wiktionary

evidence.text: The exact file page identifies 爷-bw.png as a stroke-order drawing for simplified 爷, sourced for shape and stroke order to Chinese, Taiwanese, Japanese and Hong Kong standards. It is a modern schematic, not an artifact image. The page offers GFDL 1.2+ and CC BY 3.0; selected direct image URL is https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/b/b5/%E7%88%B7-bw.png. The direct-image click failed with a cache miss, so its pixels were not inspected here.
evidence.title: File:爷-bw.png - Wikimedia Commons

evidence.text: The official interface explains that it provides per-ideograph Unihan property data, including readings, and that users can look up a character by hexadecimal code point. The requested direct individual records for 爺, 爷, 父 and 耶 could not be opened, so this general page does not verify their exact kMandarin values.

search_audit.query: Baxter Sagart readings 爺 耶 Old Chinese pronunciation
search_audit.outcome: Inspected summaries for both characters. Zhengzhang 2003 gives 爺 and 耶 /*laː/; 耶 is also listed with Middle Chinese Baxter yae. No primary source establishing a Baxter–Sagart reconstruction for this pair was found in the accessible results.
Cross-checked the same-system Zhengzhang-series listing: 耶 (*laː) series includes 爺. This supports the phonetic-series comparison but remains secondary reporting.

search_audit.query: Unicode Unihan Database Lookup official per-character records
search_audit.outcome: Opened official interface documentation successfully. Direct official lookups for all four requested code points were inaccessible via the web tool.
Inspected 爺 and 耶 pages. The pages report Zhengzhang /*laː/ for both, but the Old Chinese basic-vocabulary appendix did not contain either as a direct primary reconstruction source.

gaps: No independently verified oracle-bone, bronze, bamboo/slip, seal-script or dated inscription image for 爺 was found. Do not state a first-creation date, an Eastern Han origin, or a specific seal-to-clerical graphic path from this evidence.

The CUHK entry cites Mulan Poetry but does not directly establish the poem’s composition date, earliest surviving witness, or whether the graph was 爺 or 耶 in early textual witnesses. Its listed semantic uses are not a complete chronological sequence. The cited Tang and Ming sources are dictionary-reported, not directly checked against primary editions.

CUHK supports the standard 父 + 耶 analysis. Zhengzhang 2003 summaries report the same Old Chinese reconstruction /*laː/ for host and phonetic, but no primary reconstruction volume or Baxter–Sagart local rows were checked in this run. Thus the phonetic analysis is supported by the dictionary and secondary reconstruction summary, while a primary-source historical sound derivation remains unverified.

耶’s separate graphic account as a俗字/corruption of 邪 applies to 耶 itself. Evidence does not show that 爺 is an error form, nor that 爺 is a whole-graph phonetic loan. No independent source-word/object borrowing claim requiring a depicted object’s pronunciation was established.

The harness supplied local Unihan kMandarin rows 爺 yé and 爷 yé. They were not independently inspected from local files in this browsing stage, and official per-character Unihan records for 爺 (U+723A), 爷 (U+7237), 父 (U+7236), and 耶 (U+8036) could not be opened. Unicode provides only a general lookup documentation page here.

The Commons candidate is a modern stroke-order drawing for simplified 爷 and does not explain ancient form history. Its exact direct image URL was exposed by the inspected description page, but the direct image fetch failed with cache miss; no pixel inspection is claimed. No suitable artifact glyph image with verified identity and rights was found.

The official simplified-character standard’s exact entry for 爺→爷 was not inspected; the classification relies on a secondary dictionary statement and the dossier’s traditional/simplified counterpart metadata.
